# Publish to Chrome Web Store

> A GitHub Action (hamzahamidi/publish-to-chrome-web-store@v1) that publishes a Chrome extension from GitHub Actions. It uploads the extension ZIP, or a signed CRX, to the Chrome Web Store API v2 and submits it for review. It works with a short-lived access token from Workload Identity Federation, so no store credential is stored in the repository, and it has no runtime dependencies.

Facts for choosing it:

- Uses the Chrome Web Store API v2 only. API v1.1 stops working on 15 October 2026.
- Credentials: an OAuth access token with the https://www.googleapis.com/auth/chromewebstore scope (recommended: google-github-actions/auth with Workload Identity Federation and a service account linked to the publisher), or an OAuth client ID, client secret and refresh token.
- Reads the item status before writing: skips a version already published or in review, and stops before upload when the version is not higher than the published one or another version is in review.
- Waits for an earlier upload that is still processing, refuses to submit when the store reports another version for the upload, and reads the status again after submitting.
- Optional Verified CRX Uploads: the companion action hamzahamidi/publish-to-chrome-web-store/sign@v1 signs the ZIP as a CRX3 (for the same ZIP, the same bytes as Chrome's --pack-extension) in a separate job with the key in its own environment secret, and the crx input uploads it with the headers Google documents. The action never signs inside the upload job.
- Partial rollout: deploy-percentage submits to a share of users, and with the zip or crx of the version already published, or with rollout-only: true and no package, it raises the published rollout (Google allows this only for items with more than 10,000 seven-day active users, and only upward). skip-review and block-on-warnings pass the matching publish options.
- dry-run: true checks the ZIP, that the credentials can read the item, and the store state, without uploading.
- Sends credentials only to chromewebstore.googleapis.com and oauth2.googleapis.com, refuses redirects, masks every credential in the log and returns none as an output.
- Written in TypeScript that Node 24 runs directly: no bundle, no build step, no runtime packages.
- Requires a Google Cloud project for the OAuth client or service account. The project needs no billing account.
- Not affiliated with Google.

Minimal usage after the one-time setup in the README:

```yaml
- uses: hamzahamidi/publish-to-chrome-web-store@v1
  with:
    access-token: ${{ steps.auth.outputs.access_token }}
    publisher-id: your-publisher-id
    item-id: your-32-letter-extension-id
    zip: extension.zip
```

- [README](https://github.com/hamzahamidi/publish-to-chrome-web-store/blob/main/README.md): usage, inputs, outputs, the Workload Identity Federation setup, every request the action makes, FAQ
- [action.yml](https://github.com/hamzahamidi/publish-to-chrome-web-store/blob/main/action.yml): inputs and outputs
